title: Multi-ring-oscillator XOR entropy source (N-way parallel jitter combining)
topology: N independent free-running ring oscillators whose outputs are combined by a single XOR tree (a "parallel oscillator ring" entropy source) and then sampled by a slow reference clock. Each ring contributes independent phase jitter; XOR-ing many nominally independent jittery edges accumulates their entropy so that the sampled bit is unpredictable even when any one ring's per-sample jitter is small. This is the architecture that hardens the single-RO baseline: rather than relying on one oscillator accumulating enough jitter over a long sampling interval, it sums entropy spatially across N oscillators so a shorter sampling interval (higher throughput) still yields adequate per-bit min-entropy, and the failure of a single ring degrades rather than destroys the source. It is the topology used by open-silicon entropy sources such as OpenTitan's, which instantiate multiple ring oscillators feeding a digital conditioning and health-test pipeline.
spec_class: hardware security primitive — true-random-number-generator (TRNG) noise/entropy source for cryptographic key generation, nonces, and DRBG seeding, targeting a validated SP 800-90B min-entropy rate at usable throughput; the design must supply raw entropy plus health-testable conditioning, not any analog-precision or signal-integrity spec

pdk_portability.notes: The N-oscillator + XOR-tree structure is fully digital-standard-cell portable: it needs only inverters/NANDs, an XOR tree, and sampling flip-flops, all in sky130's standard-cell library (sky130_fd_sc_hd) and every digital CMOS PDK. What is PDK- and layout-dependent is (a) each ring's absolute jitter and frequency, which set how many rings N are needed to reach a target min-entropy, and (b) the independence assumption between rings, which physical proximity and shared supply can violate on any node via injection locking / mutual pulling. Re-characterize per-ring jitter and inter-ring correlation on sky130 silicon across corners; do not port an N value or an entropy estimate from another process or FPGA implementation, since the required N scales inversely with per-ring jitter and correlated rings do not add entropy.

sizing_approach: The load-bearing sizing decision is N, the number of parallel rings, versus the available per-ring jitter. Sunar, Martin, and Stinson give the canonical provable-security framework: model each ring's sampled edge as a jittery signal, require the XOR combination to reach a target entropy, and derive the minimum N from the per-ring jitter magnitude relative to the sampling period — lower per-ring jitter (or a shorter, higher-throughput sampling interval) demands proportionally more rings, and their analysis fixes N and the post-XOR sampling/resampling so the design meets a bound rather than an empirical guess. Practically: characterize a single ring's accumulated-jitter standard deviation on real silicon at the worst (lowest-jitter, fastest) corner; use the Sunar et al. bound to pick N with margin; use distinct stage counts / lengths across the rings so their nominal frequencies differ and they are less prone to mutually injection-lock into a correlated (entropy-collapsing) mode; then validate the achieved SP 800-90B min-entropy on the raw combined stream, since correlated rings and deterministic coupling both inflate an unvalidated estimate. Size for the worst corner and let continuous health tests catch entropy shortfalls.
layout_idioms: physically separate the N rings and vary their stage counts/orientations so they do not injection-lock into a common frequency; correlated rings contribute no additional independent entropy no matter how many are XOR-ed
per-ring or well-isolated supply decoupling plus guard rings so a shared periodic aggressor cannot lock multiple rings simultaneously and collapse their combined entropy
balanced XOR-tree routing so no single ring's edge dominates the combined signal's timing, keeping each ring's jitter contribution comparable at the sampling flip-flop

expose a raw-noise-source tap ahead of the conditioning function (per SP 800-90B) so the combined entropy source can be validated on silicon independently of the conditioner, and route each ring's enable so rings can be individually toggled for per-ring characterization and defect isolation
place the SP 800-90B health-test logic (Repetition Count Test, Adaptive Proportion Test) on the raw sampled stream close to the sampler so a degraded source is detected before conditioning masks it

source.citation: B. Sunar, W. J. Martin, and D. R. Stinson, "A Provably Secure True Random Number Generator with Built-In Tolerance to Active Attacks," IEEE Transactions on Computers, vol. 56, no. 1, pp. 109-119, Jan. 2007 (author-hosted preprint publicly available). Open-silicon reference architecture: lowRISC/OpenTitan entropy_src and RNG documentation, Apache-2.0. Health-testing/architecture guidance: E. Barker et al., NIST Special Publication 800-90B, January 2018.
source.license_or_openness: Sunar-Martin-Stinson is cited for its provable-security N-versus-jitter sizing framework and methodology only (no figures or text reproduced); an author-hosted preprint is publicly available (case 1 open-access), with the IEEE Transactions version behind a subscription (case 2). OpenTitan's entropy source is Apache-2.0-licensed open silicon whose documented multi-RO + conditioning architecture is cited as an open reference implementation (case 3). NIST SP 800-90B is a public-domain U.S. government standard. No proprietary or NDA'd data is recorded.

notes: This is the parallel-array architecture the fleet adopted, so getting N right for the available per-ring jitter is the central design task — under-provisioning N silently ships a source that passes statistical smoke tests but falls short of its claimed min-entropy at the worst corner. The raw XOR-combined stream still requires conditioning (a vetted cryptographic conditioning function, or an extractor) and always-on SP 800-90B health testing (RCT + APT) on the raw samples, with a raw-tap access path for silicon validation. For the single-oscillator baseline this generalizes, see ring-oscillator-jitter-trng; for a non-oscillator entropy mechanism see metastability-trng.
